source.title: Stochastic gradient descent with random label noises: doubly stochastic models and inference stabilizer
source.authors: Haoyi Xiong; Xu-Hong Li; Bo Yu; Dong-Rui Wu; Zhan-Xing Zhu; D. Dou

record.tranche_reason: Reports how unbiased label noise during self-distillation affects gradient norms, validation accuracy, and test accuracy in ResNet-56; this is an extension to noisy self-distillation, not a direct test of the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study does not test random-label memorization, natural-label training under standard recipes, width sweeps, convolution-versus-fully-connected comparisons, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Its measured gradient norm is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7. Results on noisy self-distillation and linear regression are adjacent findings recorded under versions none.
record.test_reason: The study tests implicit regularization from noisy self-distillation and SGD dynamics in linear regression, but none of V1–V8. Output-gradient norms and qualitative flatness descriptions do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled sharpness or its association with generalization gaps. Batch size is fixed in the experiments, so the theoretical dependence on batch size does not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors model an additional noise term from label noise and mini-batch sampling, interpret it as favoring smaller output-gradient norms and greater inference stability, and report improved self-distillation performance in some settings. Symmetric swapping changes the expected teacher logits, so its noise is unbiased around that changed target rather than around the original logits.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical deep-network method is noisy self-distillation from a trained teacher, with additive Gaussian or symmetric logit noise; the linear-regression experiment uses synthetic data and SGD trajectories. The paper does not test the original claim's random-label memorization setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and noise type/scale vary in the self-distillation experiments; label-noise variance and data covariance vary in linear regression. Gradient norms decrease with increasing noise scales, and the reported better generalization for symmetric noise is especially noted on CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: Average squared output-gradient norms decrease as Gaussian noise variance or symmetric-swap probability increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In ResNet-56 self-distillation on SVHN, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, stronger output-noise interventions reduce average squared parameter gradients of model outputs, interpreted as increased inference stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Some noisy students outperform teachers or noiseless students, and validation accuracy can guide noise selection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitably selected noisy self-distillation settings can improve held-out classification accuracy in the tested ResNet-56 workloads.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report near-zero training losses and better generalization with symmetric noise, especially on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Validation-selected symmetric-noise self-distillation can improve generalization despite similarly low final training losses; the authors interpret its solutions as flatter without measuring magnitude-aware sharpness.

fits_no_version.finding: The synthetic OLS experiments report convergence distributions centered near the optimum, with span and orientation varying with label-noise variance and data covariance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested synthetic OLS settings, label noise and data covariance alter SGD parameter-trajectory distributions.

record.code_released: All codes will be released after acceptance.
record.problems: Deep-network accuracy and gradient-norm curves are presented in figures without exact numerical values in the text; the prose reports only that some models improve. The deep-network experiment uses noisy self-distillation with teacher logits and a training/validation split, so it does not directly test the claim's natural-label versus random-label comparison. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the plotted Gaussian-versus-symmetric accuracy curves at each noise scale, or per-epoch loss trajectories, because the text does not supply recoverable individual values and the report states only aggregate qualitative trends. Figures 1 and 2 contain those plots.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe, and chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization and the effects of tuning or optimizer adaptations.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout comparisons, small-data regimes, excessive dropout, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining to measure test-accuracy changes.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the reader's tests/T3 classification to discusses/T6. All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not deny the adjacent findings. Exact curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied text, and the omitted curve-level results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Whether networks that fit random labels generalize on natural labels, and whether random-label test accuracy stays at chance.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation and weight decay.
The study measures gradient norms and discusses inference stability, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps against the tested norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.
